// Package badvaluereffixture is a synthetic KNOWN-BAD fixture for
// qdrant_client_convergence_test.go's
// TestQdrantClientConstructedOnlyByNewQdrantClient. Scanned under the
// display path "internal/example/valueref_test.go", it covers the
// function-value-alias bypass named in 01-REVIEW.md WR-01: binding the raw
// qdrant.NewClient constructor to a package-level var, then calling it
// through that var — `dial(cfg)` — rather than through the qualified
// selector `qdrant.NewClient(cfg)` a plain CallExpr-shape scanner expects.
// The `dial(cfg)` call itself stays invisible to a CallExpr scan forever
// (call.Fun is a bare *ast.Ident, never a *ast.SelectorExpr) — what this
// fixture proves is that the point where the raw constructor escapes AS A
// VALUE is caught instead. Must scan dirty with exactly one finding,
// package-level.
//
// This file carries a .go.txt extension deliberately: it is parsed from
// source bytes by go/parser, never built by `go build`/gofmt/go vet/the
// linter, so it is not swept by any of them.
package badvaluereffixture

import (
	"github.com/qdrant/go-client/qdrant"
)

// dial aliases the raw constructor as a value — the bypass this fixture
// exercises.
var dial = qdrant.NewClient

func useDial(host string, port int) (*qdrant.Client, error) {
	return dial(&qdrant.Config{Host: host, Port: port})
}
